line: This paper examines the issue of power flow in electrical circuits,  -  focusing on situations where power surges occur in the opposite direction to traditional flow – a phenomenon known as inverse power flow. This unconventional problem has gained significance due to the increasing integration of distributed generation units,  -  solar panels, into power systems. The study introduces a comprehensive mathematical model,  -  constraints on voltage and power limits, and proposes an efficient solution method based on optimization algorithms, to determine the pattern of inverse power flow. Case studies conducted in this research highlight the real-world implications and potential for the management of power systems. And pave the way for more precise and efficient manipulation of power flow in complex electrical grids. Future implications of managing inverse power flow and its importance in the development of smart grid technologies are also explored.

Georgia's government has announced plans to introduce a hidden asset pardon, allowing individuals to declare any undisclosed assets without facing criminal charges. This move is part of the country's ongoing efforts to combat corruption and promote transparency.  Under the proposed scheme, individuals who voluntarily disclose their hidden assets will be exempt from prosecution, and will only be required to pay a fine. The fine will be based on the value of the assets declared, with higher penalties for larger amounts.  The government hopes the hidden asset pardon will encourage individuals to come forward and declare any undisclosed wealth, thereby increasing tax revenues and reducing corruption. It is estimated that billions of dollars are hidden in offshore accounts and other undisclosed assets in Georgia.  The initiative is part of a broader anti-corruption campaign launched by the government. Which has been praised by international organizations  -  Transparency International. Georgia has made significant progress , in recent years, in tackling corruption and improving its business environment. But hidden assets remain a major challenge.  Critics argue that the hidden asset pardon could be seen as a lenient approach, , towards individuals who have evaded taxes and engaged in corrupt practices. They argue that a more stringent approach. Including criminal charges and asset seizures, would be more effective in deterring such behavior.  However, supporters of the scheme believe that it strikes a balance between encouraging individuals to come forward and punishing those who continue to hide their assets. They argue that the prospect of avoiding criminal charges and paying a fine will incentivize individuals to disclose their hidden wealth, leading to increased tax revenues and a more transparent economy.  The government plans to launch an awareness campaign to inform the public about the hidden asset pardon and the benefits of coming forward. It will also establish a dedicated unit within the tax authorities to handle the disclosure process and ensure that individuals are treated fairly.  The introduction of the hidden asset pardon is seen as a significant step towards strengthening Georgia's anti-corruption efforts and promoting a more transparent business environment. It remains to be seen how effective the scheme will be in encouraging individuals to disclose their hidden assets and whether it will have a lasting impact on reducing corruption in the country.

> 8-1/2 cups water, divided > 4 small carrots, chopped > 3 stalks celery, diced > 4 cloves garlic, minced > 2 leeks (white part only) cut into pieces > 6 (6 oz.) packages fresh baby spinach leaves > One 4 lb turkey, cooked and diced or shredded > 8 tomatos (or equivalent amount frozen tomatoes) > 2 tsp dried rosemary > 2 bay leaves > Salt & Pepper to taste > Corn meal noodles combine in food processor mix 1 cup cornmeal, 1 teaspoon salt and 4 cups hot tap water; pulse mixture until dough comes together then set aside for 5 minutes. Dust countertop with flour and corn flour. Roll out cornmeal dough as if rolling out pie crust. Cut in strips either by hand or scissors about an inch thick. Bring each strip up at one end like you were making lasagna. Cover pan lightly. Set apart while working on vegetable soup and cooking your broth/stock. Cooking broth: In a large stockpot melt coconut oil over medium heat. Saute garlic until light golden, being careful not to burn it. Add remaining vegetables including herbs. Bring to boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer until tender about 20-30 minutes. Strain through a colander, discard solids and use the juice as the base for the soup if desired. Add more filtered water, organic chicken base and season lightly. Add the meat. Put the noodles into a bowl, arrange the vegetables and place the meat in the center. Put the broth around the edge. Garnish with additional salt, pepper and parsley. Serve immediately.

Selective Publication in Nature: An Empirical Analysis of Abstracts from the Journal of Statistical Genetics Abstract, We investigate selective publication of papers in Nature Genetics. On one side we analyze the frequency of abstracts in Nature Genetics articles using a logistic regression model, finding significant differences by author, issue and field; No significant difference is observed between journals. On the other hand, we compare publications based on geographic location and type of journal issue (only or top specialization); Similar results are presented; New analyses and possible explanations are discussed; The first part of the analysis is performed using a logistic regression model. Two hypotheses for potential effects are proposed  -  (i) journals tend to publish manuscripts of the same quality in the same field, and (ii) journals publish only manuscripts with no papers or few original articles. In the second part, we examine manuscripts by author, issue and geographic region. It is shown that patterns differ for abstracts versus no abstracts, controlled for publication status and authorship and geographic location. The study will be discussed at a conference in October 2014.

The novel chronicles Stevens, a butler at Darlington Hall who has dedicated his life to serving his master Lord Darlington. Set in the 1930s, the story begins with Stevens in his mid-50s and has been working at Darlington Hall for over 30 years. He is deeply devoted to his work and takes great pride in his profession, believing that a butler's role extends beyond mere service to provide continuity and tradition in an evolving world.  Despite his dedication, Stevens faces numerous challenges. He has few close relationships outside of work and his only companion is his father, who is also a butler at a nearby estate. As the novel progresses, Stevens's father becomes ill, forcing him to confront the reality of his own mortality and the choices he has made in life.  Simultaneously, Stevens finds himself entangled in events that challenge his beliefs about his role as a butler and his relationship with his master. Lord Darlington, a wealthy and influential man, is a Nazi sympathizer, prompting Stevens to grapple with moral implications of serving such a man. As political tensions escalate in Europe, Stevens must decide where his loyalties truly lie and what he is willing to do to uphold his sense of duty and honor.  Throughout the novel, Stevens grapples with questions of identity, loyalty and morality all against the backdrop of rapidly changing times in the 1930s. Reflecting on his life and past decisions, he confronts both personal and historical legacies. The narrative explores profound themes of human nature, duty, loyalty and identity, offering a poignant and thought-provoking examination of the human condition.

Prime Minister Boris Johnson announced his resignation from his position in June, marking the end of his three-year leadership of the United Kingdom.  In a statement delivered outside 10 Downing Street, Johnson informed the Queen of his decision earlier in the day. He expressed gratitude for the opportunity to serve and acknowledged the weight of responsibility that comes with being prime minister.  "It has been an immense privilege to serve as your prime minister," Johnson said. "I have always tried my best to live up to the trust placed in me by the British people and to do what I believe is right for our country."  Johnson's departure comes amid mounting pressure following a series of scandals and controversies that have marred his time in office. A growing number of Conservative MPs had called for his resignation, citing concerns over his leadership style and handling of key issues, including Brexit and the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. The Lobster is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores the complexities of human relationships and societal norms. Set in a dystopian future, the movie presents a world where single people are forced to find a partner within 45 days or be transformed into an animal of their choice. The film's premise may seem absurd at first, but it serves as a clever allegory for the pressures and expectations placed upon individuals in our society.  The movie's protagonist, David, played by Colin Farrell, is a recently divorced man struggling to cope with the new world order. He is sent to a strange hotel where he must navigate a series of bizarre rituals and encounters with other singletons, all vying for love and acceptance. The hotel's residents are a fascinatingly eccentric cast of characters, each with their own unique quirks and backstories.  The film's pacing is deliberate and measured, allowing the audience to fully absorb the eerie atmosphere and sense of unease that permeates every frame. The cinematography is stark and haunting, with a muted color palette that adds to the overall sense of bleakness. The score is equally effective, utilizing unsettling sound effects and discordant music to heighten the tension and unease.  The performances in the film are outstanding, with Colin Farrell delivering a particularly strong turn as the protagonist. His portrayal of David's desperation and confusion is both heartbreaking and uncomfortable to watch, making for a compelling and nuanced performance. The supporting cast is equally impressive, with standout performances from Rachel Weisz and Olivia Colman.  The Lobster is not an easy watch, but it is a challenging and uncomfortable film that asks difficult questions about the nature of love, relationships, and societal conformity. It is a deeply thought-provoking and intelligent work that lingers long after the credits have rolled. It is a film that will leave you questioning your own beliefs and values.

Arie Lev Gruzman (Hebrew, ארי לעבד גרוזמן, born July 1, 1948) is an American academic and scholar of Jewish studies. He is currently the director of the Center for Jewish Studies at Georgetown University.  Gruzman was born in Tel Aviv, Israel, to a family of Holocaust survivors. He received his undergraduate degree from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1969, and his Ph.D. in Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations from Harvard University in 1977.  After completing his doctorate, Gruzman held academic positions at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of California, Berkeley, before joining the faculty at Georgetown in 1985. At Georgetown, he has served as the director of the Center for Jewish Studies since 1995.  Gruzman's research interests include Jewish history, Jewish thought, and the relationship between Judaism and Christianity. He has published numerous articles and books on these topics, including "The Jews and the Dead Sea Scrolls" (1992) and "The Jewish Jesus, How Jewish Theology Influenced the New Testament" (2000).  In addition to his academic work, Gruzman has been involved in several interfaith initiatives; He has served as a consultant to the Vatican's Pontifical Council for Interreligious Dialogue, and has been a member of the National Council of Churches' Committee on Faith and Order.  Gruzman has also been active in promoting Jewish-Muslim dialogue. In 2008, he co-founded the Georgetown-Sultan Qabas University Dialogue Initiative, which brings together students and scholars from both institutions to engage in dialogue and learning about each other's faiths.  Throughout his career, Gruzman has been recognized for his contributions to Jewish studies and interfaith dialogue. In 2012, he was awarded the National Jewish Book Award for his book "The Jewish Jesus, How Jewish Theology Influenced the New Testament." He has also received numerous honors and awards from various organizations.

This paper introduces a topological image segmentation technique for automatic sign language recognition. It employs the watershed transformation to derive the topological derivative from the gradient magnitude of video frames; However, the gradient magnitude does not meet the topological derivative's requirements, so an isotropic filter is applied to normalize its values. This approach enhances the watershed-based segmentation technique's effectiveness and robustness. Subsequently, regions are classified using statistical features from the normalized RGB histogram; Feature selection is then performed using the Fisher score to reduce dimensionality and identify the most relevant features for classification. Finally, the k-NN classifier is used for the classification of gesture sequences. The proposed method has been validated using the Texas Instrument DLP Sign Language Gesture Database, achieving a recognition rate of 95.6%.

As Israel gears up for its first general election since 2019. A critical issue is filling the top management vacancies in the banking sector. Bank of Israel Governor Mark Carney, set-to leave in January next year, has announced his intention to step down. The finance ministry is now in the process of recruiting a new governor with extensive experience in leading large financial institutions and a deep understanding of the regulatory frameworks governing international trade. The ministry has its sights set on the United States, with sources close to the matter indicating that the U.S. is the top candidate. Finance Minister Yair Lapid, who met with Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell in Washington D.C., has expressed that the U.S. has provided Israel with significant support over the years. And the two countries are now in a position to work together on a strong foundation. The search for a new governor is in its early stages with some senior officials from major investment banks, including JPMorgan Chase, set-to interview for the position. It is also believed that other central bankers, such as Andy Haldane and Andrew Bailey of the Bank of England, could also be considered. Despite the ongoing tensions with the United States over Israeli settlement policies, Prime Minister Naftali Bennett has assured that the two countries' relations are strong and positive.

Ingredients, For the dumplings One 16-ounce package of square dumpling wrappers or round wrappers 1 pound crabmeat 1/2 cup all-purpose flour 2 tablespoons minced green onion 2 tablespoons minced fresh ginger 1 tablespoon soy sauce 1 tablespoon sake or dry sherry 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper 1/2 cup thinly sliced green onion tops  For the dipping sauce 1/4 cup soy sauce 1 tablespoon rice vinegar 1 tablespoon honey 1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger  Instructions 1. In a large bowl, mix together the crabmeat. Flour, minced green onion, minced ginger, soy sauce, sake or sherry, sesame oil, salt and pepper. 2. Place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper. (Save any leftover filling for another use.) 3. Dip your finger into water and moisten the edges of the wrapper. Fold opposite corners together, pressing to seal. Arrange filled dumplings on a baking sheet dusted with flour. 4. Prepare a basket steamer. Stack the dumplings touching but not overlapping. Cover and steam for about 10 minutes until the wrappers are cooked through and the filling is hot. 5. In a small bowl, mix all dipping sauce ingredients and whisk to blend. 6. Arrange hot dumplings on a plate and sprinkle with green onion tops. Serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

This study introduces two innovative methods for multi-organ segmentation using deep learning. Both techniques utilize the concept of leveraging multiple input planes as parallel channels, allowing different supervision schemes to be defined for each plane. This approach enables the information flow to better handle ambiguous signals from partial or irrelevant annotations (semi-supervision), and to enhance generalization to test images with occluded or rotated organs. The study combines a convolutional autoencoder for RGB channels to extract features and a 3D ResNet for T2w/FLAIR subtraction to convey anatomical details. This approach enables the efficient representation of both appearance and geometry using complementary domains, providing significant performance improvements over standard methods. The study's results show marked improvements over seminal MICCAI publications, with a quantitative comparison on five public datasets demonstrating that the proposed methods exceed state-of-the-art scores, achieving results comparable to human experts with a simple modification of the backbone architecture.

The South African government has announced plans to reopen its embassy in Mauritius, ending a 20-year diplomatic standoff between the two countries.  The decision was made following talks between President Cyril Ramaphosa and Prime Minister Pravind Jugnauth, who met on the sidelines of the African Union summit in Ethiopia last week.  Mauritius had accused South Africa of supporting separatist rebels in the Indian Ocean island nation during the 1980s and 1990s. This led to the closure of the South African embassy in Port Louis in 1997.  In recent years, relations between the two countries have improved significantly, with both sides working together to combat piracy and promote regional stability.  South Africa's foreign ministry said that the reopening of the embassy would help strengthen bilateral ties and boost economic cooperation between the two nations.  "We believe that this is an important step towards normalising our relationship," said spokesperson Clayson Mbatha. "It will allow us to engage more actively with each other on issues of mutual interest."  Mauritius welcomed the move, saying it hoped to deepen its engagement with South Africa, and benefit from increased trade and investment.  "This is a positive development for our region as a whole," said Foreign Affairs Minister Alain St. Ange. "We look forward to further strengthening our partnership with South Africa."

"The Last Children of Schewenborn" is a chilling post-apocalyptic novel that delves into the aftermath of a nuclear war in the small German town of Schewenborn. The narrative is told through Peter's eyes, a young boy who, along with his family, faces the devastation and scarcity of a world transformed by nuclear fallout.  The story begins with the bombs falling, destroying everything Peter has ever known. The once idyllic town is now a nightmarish wasteland where food and water are scarce, and the threat of radiation sickness looms; Peter's family, once comfortably middle class, is reduced to scavenging for survival.  As the story progresses, Peter's parents and siblings succumb to radiation sickness, leaving him and his younger sister, Lisa, as the last children of Schewenborn. Despite the bleak circumstances, Peter and Lisa display remarkable resilience and courage, clinging to each other for emotional support and working together to find food and shelter.  The novel is a stark exploration of the human capacity for survival in the face of unimaginable adversity. It also serves as a powerful warning about the devastating consequences of nuclear warfare. Despite the grim subject matter, the story is ultimately about hope, resilience, and the enduring power of the human spirit.

Flemish Beef Roast (Or Stew) with Vegetables Recipe  Ingredients 1 2-3 pound beef roast, trimmed 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 1 large onion, chopped 2 carrots, chopped - 2 celery stalks chopped 3 cloves garlic, minced 1 teaspoon dried thyme 1 teaspoon dried rosemary 2 tablespoons tomato paste 1 cup beef broth 1 cup red wine 2 cups chopped mushrooms Salt and pepper to taste  Instructions 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. 2. Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium high heat. Add beef roast and brown on all sides about 8 minutes per side. Remove and set aside. 3. Add chopped onion, carrots, celery, garlic, thyme and rosemary to pot. Cook for about 5 minutes stirring occasionally until vegetables are softened. 4. Stir in tomato paste, beef broth, red wine and mushrooms. Bring to a simmer. 5. Season beef roast with salt and pepper. Place roast back in pot, spooning vegetable mixture on top. 6. Cover pot with a lid and transfer to preheated oven. Roast for about 1 hour and 15 minutes or until beef is tender and vegetables are cooked through. 7. Remove roast from pot and let rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving. Serve with vegetable mixture on the side. Enjoy.

His contributions to the city were so significant that many buildings and facilities were named in his honor, including the James W. Truman Public School on West 123rd Street. Which opened in 1913 and continues to serve students to this day. Truman also established the James W. Truman Foundation in 1924, which continues to support educational programs in New York City to this day.

This paper introduces the concept of witness structures and immediate snapshot complexes, as a method to analyze the combinatorial structure of simplicial complexes. Witness structures are an extension of simplicial complexes that allow for representation of higher-dimensional combinatorial structures. Immediate snapshot complexes are a specific type of witness structure that capture the combinatorial structure of a system at a particular point in time. The paper presents algorithms for constructing these structures along with techniques for analyzing their properties. The authors illustrate the practical applications of these concepts through various real-world examples, including social networks and biological systems. Overall, this paper offers a novel framework for studying complex systems, and provides new insights into their behavior.

Asparagus with Prosciutto di Parma Pecorino Pepato and Poached Eggs  Ingredients  -  1 bunch asparagus (about 1 pound) 6 large eggs 4 tablespoons unsalted butter 4 thin slices prosciutto di Parma torn into pieces 1/2 cup grated Pecorino Pepato cheese 1/2 cup heavy cream 1/2 teaspoon white pepper 1/4 teaspoon salt  Instructions 1. Bring a pot of water to a boil over high heat. Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with ice water and set aside. Cut the tips off the asparagus and set aside. Cut the stalks into 1-inch pieces and set aside. Blanch the tips in the boiling water for 1 minute. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the tips to the ice water and chill for 1 minute. Drain, pat dry, and set aside. Blanch the stalks for 4 to 6 minutes or until tender. Drain, pat dry, and set aside. 2. Crack the eggs into individual ramekins or cups. Fill a large skillet with water and add the white vinegar. Bring the water to a simmer over medium heat. Carefully slide the eggs into the water and cook for 3 to 5 minutes or until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked as desired. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the eggs to a towel to drain. 3. Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the prosciutto and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until the ham is crisp. Add the asparagus and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until tender-crisp. Add the cheese and cook for 1 minute or until melted. Stir in the heavy cream, pepper and salt and cook for 1 minute or until heated through. 4. To serve, divide the asparagus and prosciutto among individual plates. Top each with a poached egg and some of the cheese sauce.  Nutrition Facts Calories, 383 Fat, 29g Cholesterol, 443mg Sodium, 1152mg Carbs, 6g Fiber, 1g Sugars, 3g Protein, 23g

I was at Salt & Straw on Division today, enjoying my usual double scoop of sea salt with caramel ribbons. When a group of about 10 people walked in, all wearing matching t shirts that said "Ice Cream Club". They were a diverse group, ranging from a 5-year old kid to an elderly woman in her 80s. They were all laughing and joking around, clearly having a great time.   They each ordered their own unique flavor. And then the oldest woman stepped forward and said, "And one pint of every flavor to go, please." The staff looked a bit taken aback, but started packing up the pints.   While they were waiting. The woman explained to the rest of us in the shop that they were part of a local ice cream club. And every month they visit a different ice cream shop, try all the flavors, and then take a pint of each flavor back to their meeting to share and rate.   I was so charmed by this idea and the joy that this group was clearly getting from their ice cream adventure. It was such a sweet reminder of the simple pleasures in life. Blue Merle was an American rock band from Los Angeles, California, United States. The band consisted of brothers Liam Finn (vocals, guitar) and Caleb Johnson (bass, keyboards) and sister Morgan Finn (drums, percussion). The band released two albums, Burning in the Sun (2003) and Keeps Me Wondering (2006) before breaking up in 2007.  Liam and Caleb Finn formed Blue Merle in 2002 after the dissolution of their previous band the Johnson Brothers. The pair were soon joined by their sister Morgan and the three began writing and performing together.  The band released their debut album, Burning in the Sun in 2003. The album was produced by T-Bone Burnett and featured the single "Halo".  The band's second album, Keeps Me Wondering, was released in 2006; The album was produced by Brendan O'Brien and featured the singles "Out of My Hands" and "Boxcar Racer".  The band toured extensively in support of both albums, performing with artists such as Bob Dylan, Sheryl Crow and John Mayer.  In 2007, the band announced that they were breaking up; Liam and Caleb Finn went on to form the band N. In a 2014 interview with The Huffington Post, Liam Finn stated that Blue Merle had "run its course" and that the band was "never really meant to be a long-term thing".

Tom Hanks has been announced as the lead actor in a biopic about Leonardo da Vinci, a celebrated artist and inventor from history. The movie will explore his life and work from his early years in Italy to his later achievements in France.  Hanks is no stranger to playing real-life figures on screen, having won critical acclaim for his portrayals in "Captain Phillips" (2013) and "A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood" (2019). He also received Oscar nominations for both roles.  The yet untitled project will be directed by David Koepp, who has directed "Jurassic Park" (1998) and "Lincoln" (2012) for which he received another Oscar nomination. Filming is expected to begin next year, with a release date set for 2023.  This isn't the first time that Hollywood has attempted to bring da Vinci's story to the big screen. In 2003, Mel Gibson starred in "The Agony and the Ecstasy" while in 1972, Charlton Heston played the artist in "Leonard, A Life of Leonard Bernstein (I)." However, it remains to be seen how this latest adaptation will differentiate itself from its predecessors.

It starts with the introduction of a new town; It is a little quaint, and people look healthy; The book is about its residents and their lives compared to how things used to be.  The novel is about a fictional detective's time and experience; He is referred to as "Detective Caul" and begins with him and his friend discovering a body in the woods. They call the police on themselves and their friend, who tells them that Caul might not be guilty. The detectives ask Caul to meet them at a tavern, but he refuses, implying he has a case. After some time, Caul shows up to the tavern and asks if the man who discovered the body is still involved in the case. The detectives agree to talk to him before arresting Caul, but after getting the information, Caul is shot in the head, solving the mystery. However, the book does not reveal who killed Caul, only hints towards the suspect. Then it jumps to the next book, where the killer is discovered, killed similarly to Caul's friend, and there is a trial; Caul is acquitted. The narrator says, "It should have ended like it did." The book ends with Caul telling his story to a class, asking two questions, which is did he kill his friend? Was a man already involved in one of his friends' murder also responsible for killing Caul?  This makes me think this is a true novel, not a cheap fantasy novel. There are elements in the writing style that make me believe it's real rather than a cheap literary novel; I believe the author, "Caul," wrote this series to get a small piece of the $3 billion and $5 billion yearly fantasy market currently enjoyed by Rowling. The author created a well-drawn version of what it would be like to be in the world of a detective. He established Caul and his friend, and what would have happened if they hadn't met.

Italy's Parmalat founder Calisto Tanzi admits to accounting errors at the dairy firm he led for three decades, apologizing for "infinite damage" caused. The firm collapsed in December when it admitted falsifying accounts by 15 billion euros. Tanzi's empire is being sold to Brazilian rival Vigor Alimentos and Asian assets are being sold. He wants to find solutions for the firm's future and make reparations, but it cannot be bailed out. Tanzi's statements come amid news of investors being given interest-free loans instead of dividends. Parmalat, Italy's largest food company, was forced into administration in December, when it failed to raise the promised funds for a bond repayment of $500 billion. At a recent meeting with Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi and other top politicians, Tanzi admitted "errors and non-transparency" in accounting practices. Berlusconi demanded more and called Tanzi's statements "insufficient," with the possibility of a ban on Tanzi's future positions at other Italian companies.

Ingredients 1 cup unsalted butter, softened 1 cup all purpose flour 1 teaspoon baking powder 1/2 teaspoon baking soda 1/4 teaspoon salt 2 cups granulated sugar 1 cup (8 oz) jam (any flavor)  For the Dough 1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. In a small bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside. 3. In a large bowl, cream the butter and sugar on medium high speed until light and fluffy, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until combined. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. 4. For the Filling 5. Divide the dough into two equal parts. Roll each portion out on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of 1/4 inch (6 mm). Cut into rounds with a 2-inch (5-cm) cookie cutter. Place half the rounds on the prepared baking sheet. 6. Top each round with 1 teaspoon of jam. Place another round on top of the jam, pressing the edges gently to seal. 7. Bake for 15 minutes or until the edges are lightly browned. Allow to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely. This paper explores resource allocation in MIMO radar systems with multiple targets for non-coherent localization. The problem is addressed as an optimization problem to minimize the mean squared error in target localization. The study examines the effects of key system parameters,  -  the number of transmit and receive antennas, the number of transmitted signals, and the sampling rate, on radar system performance. An efficient algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is proposed to solve the optimization problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed resource allocation scheme significantly enhances the radar system's localization accuracy compared to conventional methods.

Leonti Mroveli born on January 29, 1978, in Tbilisi, Georgia is a poet and musician of Georgian-Armenian descent. He grew up in Batumi, Georgia on the Black Sea coast. In an interview with Bidzina Kheiladze, Mroveli revealed that his maternal grandfather Shalva Mroveli had migrated from Armenia during the Soviet era. His paternal grandparents were forced from Nakhchivan due to Soviet atrocities against their family.  Mroveli began composing his own songs from a young age, often incorporating his refugee experiences into his music. He drew inspiration from a variety of musical styles including pop rock, jazz, funk and blues. Unlike other Georgian musicians who have adopted Western music genres for commercial success, Mroveli prefers to maintain his authenticity in sound and lyrics. His songs often have catchy melodies and meaningful lyrics that address societal issues in Georgia, such as poverty, inequality and political unrest.  Mroveli performs in Georgia and has also made appearances abroad.

This paper introduces CIDI Lung-Seg, a single-click annotation tool for automatically delineating lungs from CT scans. The tool uses a pre-trained deep learning model to identify and segment the lungs in scans with just a single click; A blinded, controlled study comparing its performance to manual annotation found high agreement (96.2% overall) and a kappa statistic of 0.87. The tool also saves significant time, with an average time saving of 87.2%. This method has the potential to greatly reduce the time required for manual lung cancer annotations.

Sir George Martin, the orchestrator of hundreds of the Beatles' recordings, passed away at the age of 90. The news has sparked a wave of emotion and retrospectives on his life and work. Sir George was a brilliant producer and a gentleman who revolutionized popular music with the artists he supported, notably The Beatles. While he earned fame and fortune it was his work with the Beatles that brought him lasting fame. He was an arranger and talent developer whose admiration and respect extended to many musicians he worked with. Despite being known as a "pop" producer his versatility is evident in his collaborations with diverse artists  -  Matt Monro, Cilla Black, Gerry and the Pacemakers, Cheap Trick and Jeff Beck.  In his autobiography Summer of Love, Sir George recounts his early years as a Decca Records clerk detailing the incredible luck and good fortune that his career turned on. He was talented, driven and hardworking. But he was also fortunate in being in the right place at the right time. Sir George was fortunate to work with the Beatles when their career took off. Despite initial skepticism, his punctuality, love for music and sense of humor won them trust and respect. He emerged as indispensable, striving to fulfill the group's vision and desire for experimentation in the recording studio. As their success soared, Martin managed ambitious projects while navigating the demands of the group's members and associates.  For more than five decades Sir George remained connected to his work with the Beatles seeking to protect and promote their artistic legacy. Given his importance to the history of popular music, it is fitting that Sir George Martin has received a variety of awards  -  knighthood and that he has left an indelible mark on the industry he helped pioneer.

Mentone is a small unincorporated community in Newton County, Texas, United States. Medical image segmentation is crucial for clinical analysis and computer aided diagnosis. Unlike 2D images, 3D medical images offer more detailed structures and robust segmentation capabilities. However, effectively utilizing the rich information in 3D medical images remains a challenge. This paper introduces UXNet, a novel deep learning architecture for 3D medical image segmentation; UXNet employs a unique upsampled encoder-decoder network with a multi level feature aggregation mechanism. This mechanism enhances the spatial information by upsampling low level features and captures complex structures by aggregating multi level features; UXNet learns more robust representations, improving segmentation accuracy; Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets including ISLES2017, LLC and SYNAPSE BREAST CT, show that UXNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code and models are available at https //github.com/CCF-Union/UXNet.

Delightful Lemon Cake Recipe  Ingredients  2 cups all purpose flour  1 ½ teaspoons baking powder, ¼ teaspoon salt -3 large eggs, room temperature  1 cup granulated sugar  2 tablespoons lemon zest, and ¾ cup fresh lemon juice  1 cup buttermilk, room temperature, ½ cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled  2 teaspoons vanilla extract  For the glaze  1 cup powdered sugar -2-3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice  Instructions, 1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and prepare a 9x13 inch baking pan by greasing it with cooking spray or butter and coating it with flour.  2. In a medium sized bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.  3. In a separate large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes using an electric mixer. Add in the lemon zest and juice and continue mixing until well incorporated.  4. Gradually add the dry ingredients into the wet mixture while alternating with the buttermilk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.  5. Stir in the melted and cooled butter and vanilla extract until fully mixed.  6. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.  7. Allow the cake to cool completely before making the glaze. To make the glaze. Whisk together the powdered sugar and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Drizzle over the cooled cake and let it set for several hours before serving. Enjoy.

Ingredients, 1 head of broccoli, cut into small florets and 3 cloves of garlic, minced and 1/2 cup of ricotta cheese, 1/4 cup of grated parmesan cheese and 1/4 cup of hot honey 8 slices of bread and 2 tablespoons of olive oil  Instructions 1. Preheat your oven to 400°F.  2. In a large bowl, mix together the broccoli florets, minced garlic, olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper.  3. Spread the broccoli mixture onto a baking sheet and roast in the oven for 20-25 minutes. Until the broccoli is tender and slightly browned.  4. While the broccoli is roasting. Prepare the ricotta mixture. In a small bowl, mix together the ricotta cheese, parmesan cheese and a pinch of salt and pepper.  5. Once the broccoli is done. Remove it from the oven and reduce the temperature to 375°F.  6. Toast the bread slices in the oven for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden.  7. Remove the bread from the oven and spread a thin layer of ricotta mixture onto each slice.  8. Top each slice of bread with a generous spoonful of roasted broccoli and a drizzle of hot honey.  9. Serve immediately and enjoy your delicious Broccoli and Garlic Ricotta Toasts with Hot Honey.

Barry Holmes triumphs in comeback victory  Barry Holmes secured a stunning comeback to win the Welsh Open snooker title in Cardiff. The world number 39 trailed 6-2 to Mark Selby in the final but won eight of the next nine frames to triumph 10-7.  It is the first ranking event success for the 41-year old from Birmingham who has now earned £200,000 in prize money this season.  "I'm over the moon it's been a great week," Holmes said. "I've been working hard on my game and it's nice to get some reward for it."  Selby, the world number two, had been in dominant form throughout the tournament and looked on course for victory when he moved 6-2 ahead. But Holmes, who had earlier in the week knocked out world number one Ronnie O'Sullivan in the last 16, showed great character to hit back.  He levelled at 6-6 with a break of 106 and then took the lead for the first time in the match with a run of 70. Selby responded with a break of 77 to make it 7-7, but Holmes took the next three frames to move within one of victory.  The Leicester player then had a chance to force a decider in the 17th frame, but missed a red with the rest when on 46; Holmes made no mistake with a break of 53 to secure the title.  "I'm gutted to lose but I've got to take my hat off to Barry, he played unbelievable," Selby said. "I had my chances in the match, but I couldn't take them. I'm sure I'll be back stronger for it."

Coconut Fudge Brownies Recipe  Ingredients 1 cup of granulated sugar, ½ cup of softened butter, ¼ cup of melted coconut oil and 2 large eggs 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour ¾ cup of unsweetened cocoa powder 2 teaspoons baking powder ½ teaspoon salt 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips ½ cup of shredded coconut  Instructions which are 1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper.  2. In a large mixing bowl, cream together the sugar, butter and coconut oil until light and fluffy. Add in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla extract.  3. In another medium sized bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt. Gradually add this dry mixture into the wet ingredients, stirring until just combined.  4. Fold in the chocolate chips and shredded coconut until evenly distributed.  5. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula or the back of a spoon. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.  6. Allow the brownies to cool completely before cutting into squares and serving. Enjoy.

This paper introduces a novel uncertainty aware self ensembling (UA SE) model for 3D left atrium segmentation in semi supervised learning. The UA SE model leverages correlations between neighboring voxels and employs a self ensemble strategy to boost the representation power of semi-supervised learning. Utilizing a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module, the model models spatial correlations and outputs an uncertainty map. Additionally, a self ensembling module is proposed that considers both labels and uncertainties by taking into account local graph structure. The model is trained semi-supervisedly, using only a small portion of labeled data for training and leveraging the remaining unlabeled data to enhance its representation power. The proposed method is evaluated on the MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset; Experimental results show the UA SE model's effectiveness compared to state of the art semi-supervised learning methods. The code and dataset are available at https, //github.com/VITA-Group/UA-SE.

This paper explores the transition of a three-dimensional (3D) topological insulator, Bi2Se3, to a two-dimensional (2D) state. Utilizing a blend of experimental and theoretical methods, we analyze Bi2Se3's electronic structure and topological characteristics as its thickness diminishes from 3D to 2D. Our findings reveal that the 3D Dirac cone transforms into a pair of 2D Dirac cones at the edges of the Brillouin zone, leading to the formation of novel topological phases. We observe topologically protected edge states on the surfaces of the 2D system which are resilient to disorder and defects. Additionally, we identify non-trivial band structure and Fermi arc behavior in the 2D states indicating the presence of non-trivial topology. This research offers new perspectives on the transition of 3D topological insulators to 2D systems and opens avenues for further investigation into low-dimensional topological phenomena.

The future of home phones seems uncertain as more people are choosing mobile phones over landlines, according to a recent survey by Ofcom. The study found that the number of UK landline calls fell by 10% in 2020, marking a significant shift in communication habits.  The report indicates that the decline in landline usage is mainly due to the growing popularity of mobile phones and digital communication platforms like WhatsApp, Skype and Zoom. These platforms offer a variety of communication options  -  voice and video calls, text messaging and file sharing, making them a more versatile alternative to traditional landlines.  Moreover, the COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the shift towards digital communication. With many people working from home and social distancing measures in place, digital platforms have become the primary means of communication for both personal and professional purposes.  Despite the decline, landlines are still used by a significant number of people, particularly the elderly and those living in rural areas with poor mobile coverage. For these individuals, landlines provide a reliable and accessible means of communication.  However, the trend towards mobile and digital communication is likely to continue, raising questions about the future of home phones. Some experts predict that landlines may eventually become obsolete. While others believe they will continue to exist in a more limited capacity.  The telecommunications industry is also responding to this change. Many companies now offer packages that include broadband and mobile services but not landline. This reflects the changing needs and preferences of consumers, who increasingly value flexibility and convenience.  In conclusion, while the future of home phones is uncertain, it is clear that the way we communicate is evolving. As technology continues to advance, it will be interesting to see how traditional communication methods like landlines adapt to the digital age.

The US government is seeking a new ruling against tobacco companies that could cost them up to $280bn (£155bn). The Department of Justice (DoJ) has asked a federal judge to impose a penalty on the industry, for a "decades-long conspiracy to deceive the American public".  The move comes after a 2020 ruling in which the tobacco industry was found guilty of violating federal racketeering laws. The DoJ now wants the companies to surrender profits made through their alleged misconduct. Which it claims spanned more than 50 years.  The case, which is one of the largest civil cases in US history, targets major tobacco companies including Philip Morris USA, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, Brown & Williamson and Lorillard Tobacco. The government alleges that these companies deliberately misled the public about the health risks associated with smoking and the addictive nature of nicotine.  The $280bn figure is based on the government's estimate of profits from cigarette sales to underage smokers and smokers who were allegedly deceived by the companies' marketing tactics. The DoJ argues that these profits were ill-gotten and should be forfeited.  The tobacco industry has strongly denied the allegations and is expected to fight the penalty. They argue that the government's case is based on a flawed interpretation of the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO), the law under which the case is being pursued.  The industry also contends that the penalty is excessive and would lead to bankruptcy for many companies, resulting in job losses and harm to the economy. They further argue that they have already paid billions in settlements to individual states, and have significantly changed their marketing practices in response to previous litigation.  The case is expected to be heard in the coming months. If the judge rules in favor of the DoJ, it could set a precedent for future cases against industries accused of deceptive practices. However, any ruling is likely to be appealed, potentially leading to years of further litigation.

This paper investigates the problem of power flow in electrical circuits, particularly focusing on situations where power surges are running counter to traditional flow directions – a phenomenon known as inverse power flow. This unconventional problem has become significant due to the increased integration of distributed generation units, such as solar panels into power systems. The study introduces a comprehensive mathematical model, including relevant constraints regarding voltage and power limits, and proposes an efficient solution method based on optimization algorithms to determine the pattern of inverse power flows. Case studies conducted within this research elucidate the real-world implications and potential for the management of power systems, and pave the way for more exact and efficient manipulation of power flow in complex electrical grids. Future implications of managing inverse power flow and its importance in the development of smart grid technologies are also explored.

In this paper, we propose a topological image segmentation technique based on the topological derivative for automatic recognition of sign language. In order to segment the input hand gesture sequences from the video sequences, we adopt the watershed transformation to obtain the topological derivative of the gradient magnitude of the video frames. Since the gradient magnitude does not satisfy the assumption of the topological derivative, we apply an isotropic filter to obtain a suitable input for the watershed transformation. The use of isotropic filter prevents the gradient from being dominated by few directions and makes the watershed based segmentation technique more effective and robust. The segmented regions are then subjected to a classification based on the statistical features extracted from the normalized RGB histogram of the regions. In the next stage, a feature selection based on the Fisher score is applied to reduce the dimensionality and to obtain a set of features that are most relevant to the classification task. Finally, the k-NN classifier is used as the classifier for the classification of the gesture sequences. The proposed method has been tested on Texas Instrument DLP Sign Language Gesture Database and has achieved a recognition rate of 95.6%.

Abstract: In this work, two novel methods are introduced to tackle the multi-organ segmentation using deep learning. Both proposed techniques exploit the idea of leveraging multiple input planes as parallel channels on which different supervision schemes can be defined so that information flow among such representations can better handle ambiguous signals coming from partial or irrelevant annotations (semi supervision) and also boost generalization to test images with occluded or rotated organs relative to training data. Specifically, instead of operating only in the spatial domain, co-training in our case is effectively achieved along both planes thanks to the combination between a convolutional autoencoder applied to extracting features from RGB channels (which mainly capture shape variations)and the application of 3D ResNets acting on a T2w/FLAIR subtraction volume used to convey anatomical details. Such components allow us to efficiently represent both appearance and geometry through complementary domains providing important contributions in terms of performance over standard approaches based on unimodal channels and end-to-end architectures. Our results show marked improvements w.r.t seminal MICCAI publications obtained applying similar algorithms. A quantitative comparison carried out on five public datasets including brain tumor slices demonstrates that by simply modifying the backbone architecture we exceed state-of-the-art scores achieving results comparable with human experts without the need for any form of interactive fine tuning.

Medical image segmentation plays a pivotal role in clinical analysis and computer-aided diagnosis. Unlike 2D images, 3D medical images possess more informative structures and afford robust segmentation. However, how to effectively explore the rich information in 3D medical images remains a challenge. In this paper, we present a novel deep learning architecture, called UXNet, for 3D medical image segmentation. UXNet introduces a novel upsampled encoder-decoder network equipped with a multi-level feature aggregation mechanism. In this paper, we present a novel uncertainty-aware self-ensembling (UA-SE) model for semi-supervised learning of 3D left atrium segmentation. The UA-SE model exploits the correlations between neighboring voxels and uses a self-ensemble strategy to enhance the representation power of semi-supervised learning. We employ a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module to model the spatial correlations and output the uncertainty map. Furthermore, we propose a self-ensembling module that can model both the label and uncertainty simultaneously by considering the local graph structure. The proposed model is trained in a semi-supervised manner, where only a small portion of the labeled data is used for training, and the remaining unlabeled data are utilized to enhance the model's representation power. We evaluate the proposed method on the publicly available MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UA-SE model compared to the state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning methods. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/VITA-Group/UA-SE.

In this paper, we investigate the crossover of a three-dimensional (3D) topological insulator, Bi2Se3, to the two-dimensional (2D) limit. By employing a combination of experimental and theoretical techniques, we study the electronic structure and topological properties of Bi2Se3 as the thickness of the material is reduced from 3D to 2D. Our results show that the 3D Dirac cone of Bi2Se3 collapses into a pair of 2D Dirac cones at the edges of the Brillouin zone, resulting in the emergence of novel topological phases. We observe the presence of topologically protected edge states on the surfaces of the 2D system, which are robust against disorder and defects. Furthermore, we find that the 2D states exhibit non-trivial band structure and Fermi arc behavior, indicating the presence of nontrivial topology. Our work provides new insights into the crossover of 3D topological insulators to 2D systems and paves the way for further exploration of low-dimensional topological phenomena.

Raised in the tranquil beauty of the Summer Country, Princess Guenevere has had a charmed and contented life until the sudden, violent death of her mother, Queen Maire, leaves the Summer Country teetering on the brink of anarchy. Only the miraculous arrival of Arthur, heir to the Pendragon dynasty, allows Guenevere to claim her mother's throne. Smitten by the bold, sensuous princess, Arthur offers to marry her and unite their territories, while still allowing her to rule in her own right. Their love match creates the largest and most powerful kingdom in the isles. Arthur's glorious rule begins to crumble, however, when he is reunited with his mother and his long-lost half-sisters, Morgause and Morgan. Before Arthur's birth, his father - the savage and unscrupulous King Uther - banished his wife's young daughters, selling Morgause into a cruel marriage and imprisoning Morgan in a far-off convent. Both daughters have reason to avenge their suffering, but only one will strike the deadliest blows against the King and Queen, using her evil enchantments to destroy all Guenevere holds dear. When the Queen flees to Avalon, even her marriage with Arthur comes under threat. In the chaos that follows, a new young knight comes to Arthur's court to offer his services to the Queen. Her loyalty to Arthur betrayed, Guenevere falls in love with Lancelot, a love that may spell ruin for Camelot.

line: A European Parliament committee has ordered a rewrite of the proposals for controversial new European Union rules which govern computer-based inventions.
next_line: The Legal Affairs Committee (JURI) said the Commission should re-submit the Computer Implemented Inventions Directive after MEPs failed to back it. It has had vocal critics who say it could favour large over small firms and impact open-source software innovation. Supporters say it would let firms protect their inventions. The directive is intended to offer patent protection to inventions that use software to achieve their effect, in other words, "computer implemented invention". The draft law suffered setbacks when Poland, one of the largest EU member states, rejected its adoption twice in two months. Intense lobbying on the issue has started to gain momentum in some national parliaments putting them under immense pressure. Only two MEPs backed the draft law at the JURI meeting, with one voting to abstain.

line: Mary Jane Blige (; born January 11, 1971) is an American singer, songwriter and actress. Often referred to as the "Queen of Hip-Hop Soul", Blige has won nine Grammy Awards, four American Music Awards, and ten Billboard Music Awards. She has been nominated for three Golden Globe Awards and two Academy Awards, including one for her supporting role in the film Mudbound (2017) and another for its original song "Mighty River", becoming the first person nominated for acting and songwriting in the same year. Her career began in 1991 when she was signed to Uptown Records. In 1992, Blige released her debut album, What's the 411?, which is credited for introducing the mix of R&B and hip hop into mainstream pop culture. Its 1993 remix album became the first album by a singer to have a rapper on every song, popularizing rap as a featuring act. Both What's the 411? and her 1994 album My Life are featured on the Rolling Stones 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list, and the latter on Time magazine's All-Time 100 Albums. Throughout her career, Blige went on to release 14 studio albums, all of which have reached the top ten on the Billboard 200 chart, including four number-one albums. Her biggest hits include "Real Love", "Not Gon' Cry", "Be Without You" and the Billboard Hot 100 number-one single "Family Affair".

She has been nominated for three Golden Globe Awards and two Academy Awards, including one for her supporting role in the film Mudbound (2017) and another for its original song "Mighty River", becoming the first person nominated for acting and songwriting in the same year. Her career began in 1991 when she was signed to Uptown Records. In 1992, Blige released her debut album, What's the 411?, which is credited for introducing the mix of R&B and hip hop into mainstream pop culture. Its 1993 remix album became the first album by a singer to have a rapper on every song, popularizing rap as a featuring act. Both What's the 411? and her 1994 album My Life are featured on the Rolling Stones 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list, and the latter on Time magazine's All-Time 100 Albums. Throughout her career, Blige went on to release 14 studio albums, all of which have reached the top ten on the Billboard 200 chart, including four number-one albums. Her biggest hits include "Real Love", "Not Gon' Cry", "Be Without You" and the Billboard Hot 100 number-one single "Family Affair".

line: Princess Taramis of Shadizar promises to bring Conan's lost love Valeria back to life if the Cimmerian will procure two magical items that she hopes will gain her ultimate power, a wizard's gem and a horn that can awaken the dreaming god Dagoth. He undertakes the quest together with his thief partner Malak and Taramis' niece Jehnna and henchman Bombaata. On their journey they are joined by two additional allies whom Conan saves from dire fates; the magician Akiro and the female warrior Zula. At their goal, the castle of the wizard Amon-Rama, Jehnna is kidnapped. Thanks to Akiro's magic she is located in Amon-Rama's lair and a way in is discovered. Inside, Conan is separated from the others and forced to battle a Man-Ape in a hall of mirrors, which he is only able to defeat by destroying the mirrors. He also mortally wounds the wizard, who is hiding behind one of them. Jehnna, who is the only person who can safely handle the wizard's gem, retrieves the first magical item. Afterwards the group beats off an attack by Corinthian soldiers, and continues on to the fortress that holds the horn. It is retrieved at the cost of a battle with its Dagoth-worshipping keepers, whose leader Akiro defeats in a sorcerous duel. Bombaata and Jehnna escape through a tunnel, which the former closes to the others by starting a landslide. Back at Taramis' palace, the queen conducts a ritual to awaken Dagoth that entails the placing of the horn on the forehead of the sleeping deity, and ultimately the sacrifice of Jehnna. Conan, Akiro and Zula, having survived the landslide, interrupt the proceedings. Conan fights and defeats Bombaata while Zula rescues Jehnna. In the absence of the sacrifice, Dagoth is an uncontrollable monster on his revival, eating Taramis and threatening the destruction of everything else. On the advice of Akiro, Conan rips the horn from Dagoth's forehead, and the creature finally falls. In the aftermath, Jehnna succeeds to the throne of Shadazar and takes Zula, Akiro, and Malak as advisors. She offers Conan her hand and a place at her side as king, but the Cimmerian prefers to win his own kingdom.

Lorenzo "Ka Tanny" Martinez Tañada Sr. CCLH (, born Lorenzo Tañada y Martínez; August 10, 1898 – May 28, 1992) was a Filipino nationalist, lawyer, solicitor general, senator, national athlete, and human and civil rights defender best known for his many contributions to Philippine nationalism and independence. As first post-war solicitor general, longest serving senator for 24 years, and staunch opposition to martial law under Ferdinand Marcos. He is also equally renowned for his efforts to stop the continued presence of US military bases in the Philippines through the Anti-Bases Coalition (ABC). Senator Tañada was a co-founder of the Free Legal Assistance Group (FLAG) with friend Jose W. Diokno. FLAG is the largest group of human rights lawyers nationwide. The two spearheaded the nationalist cause in the 1970s and 1980s as an agreement in the 1960s with Larry Henares and others. Tañada was also the chairman of the Justice for Aquino, Justice for All (JAJA) movement that sought to oust Marcos after the assassination of former Sen. Ninoy Aquino. He was also the founding chairman of a merged party called Bayan that opposed Marcos in the 1978 elections, and he founded the Nuclear-Free Philippines Coalition or NFPC, which successfully prevented the opening of the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant under the Marcos administration. Serving in the Philippine Senate for 24 years beginning in 1947 up until 1971, he is the longest-serving senator in Philippine history and is referred to as the "Grand Old Man of Philippine Politics." In his youth, he was also a national football team goalkeeper and was part of the Philippine national team that bagged silver medals at the 1923 and 1925 Far Eastern Championship Games, the precursor to the famous Asian Games.

The Remains of the Day tells, in first person, the story of Stevens, an English butler who has dedicated his life to the loyal service of Lord Darlington (mentioned in increasing detail in flashbacks). The novel begins with Stevens receiving a letter from a former colleague, Miss Kenton, describing her married life, which he believes hints at an unhappy marriage. The receipt of the letter coincides with Stevens having the opportunity to revisit this once-cherished relationship, if only under the guise of investigating the possibility of re-employment. Stevens's new employer, a wealthy American named Mr Farraday, encourages Stevens to borrow his car to take a well-earned break, a "motoring trip". As he sets out, Stevens has the opportunity to reflect on his immutable loyalty to Lord Darlington, on the meaning of the term "dignity", and even on his relationship with his own late father. Ultimately Stevens is forced to ponder the true nature of his relationship with Miss Kenton. As the book progresses, increasing evidence of Miss Kenton's one-time love for Stevens, and of his for her, is revealed. Working together during the years leading up to the Second World War, Stevens and Miss Kenton fail to admit their true feelings towards each other. All of their recollected conversations show a professional friendship which at times came close to crossing the line into romance, but never dared to do so. Miss Kenton, it later emerges, has been married for over 20 years and therefore is no longer Miss Kenton but has become Mrs Benn. She admits to wondering occasionally what a life with Stevens might have been like, but she has come to love her husband and is looking forward to the birth of their first grandchild. Stevens muses over lost opportunities, both with Miss Kenton and with his long-time employer, Lord Darlington. At the end of the novel, Stevens instead focuses on the "remains of [his] day", referring to his future service with Mr Farraday.

next_line: The country's new president, Mikhail Saakashvili, has said that anyone now willing to disclose their wealth will only have to pay 1% in income tax. The measure is designed to legitimise previously hidden economic activity and boost Georgia's flagging economy. Georgia's black market is estimated to be twice the size of its legal economy.

line: By declaring their assets and paying the one-off tax, people would be able to "legalise their property", Mr Saakashvili stressed.
previous_line: The new government is encouraging companies to pay taxes by scrapping existing corruption investigations and destroying all tax records from before 1 January, three days before President Saakashvili was elected. "Documentation about where this money came from doesn't exist because under the former, entirely warped regime, earning capital honestly was not possible."
next_line: "No one will have the right to check this money's origin. This money must go back into the economy." line: Edwin Bryant (August 21, 1805 – December 16, 1869) was a Kentucky newspaper editor whose popular 1848 book What I Saw in California describes his overland journey to California, his account of the infamous Donner Party, and his term as second alcalde, or pre-statehood mayor, of the city of San Francisco. Early life and newspaper career
next_line: Bryant was born in Pelham, Massachusetts, the son of the first cousins Ichabod Bryant and Silence Bryant. He studied medicine under his uncle, Dr. Peter Bryant, father of the poet William Cullen Bryant.  He may have attended Brown University.  He founded the Providence, Rhode Island newspaper the Literary Cadet  in 1826 and edited the New York Examiner in Rochester, New York.

Mentone  is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Loving County, Texas, United States. As the county's only community, it serves as the county seat and had a 2010 population of 19, almost a quarter of the county's 82 people at the time. Mentone was, until recent years, the least-populated unincorporated county seat in the United States, but lost that distinction with the 2010 census to Gann Valley, South Dakota, which had a population of 14. Mentone was designated a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark in 1967 as the "Smallest County Seat in Texas". History
next_line: Named after Menton, France, by a French surveyor, present-day Mentone is actually the second such named community in Loving County; an earlier Mentone was founded south of the current town in 1893, but was abandoned in 1905. A second town on that site was called Juanita and then Porterville, but was deserted anew when Mentone was re-established in 1931, with most residents moving to the new town.  The town on the current site was named Ramsey before being renamed. During its heyday, Mentone boasted five cafes, five gas stations, two hotels, two drugstores, two recreation halls, two barbershops, a dance hall, a machine shop, and a dry cleaner. It also had its own newspaper, the Mentone Monitor, which published from 1932 to 1935. After reaching a high population mark around 600 residents in the 1930s, the population has declined ever since, and in 2000, it had only 15 people, "more or less", according to National Geographic (the total population of Loving County itself (as of 2010) was 82.)

line: In recent years, the career of Detective Chief Inspector Alan Banks has been stalled-and, in fact, very nearly destroyed-by the petty animosities of his politically ambitious senior officer Chief Constable Riddle. But when nude pictures of Riddle’s runaway teenage daughter show up on a pornographic Web site, he turns to Banks for help. The trail leads Banks first to London’s Soho, an area of strip clubs and sex shops, then to the upmarket Little Venice, where Emily Riddle is living with a dangerous gangster with ties to world of rock music. At first she refuses to come home, but later Emily turns up at Banks’s hotel, bruised and frightened and asking for his help. Soon she is back with her family in Yorkshire, and Banks’s work appears to be done. Other concerns occupy Banks’s time. A major reorganization and expansion of Eastvale Regional Headquarters has brought Detective Sergeant Annie Cabbot back into his life, and she soon finds demons of her own to face. As they begin an investigation into the slaying of Charlie Courage, a low-level petty crook, a murder occurs at an Eastvale nightclub, filling the tabloids with headlines that scream of scandal, sex and high-level corruption. It is a cold and savage homicide that shakes Banks to his core, and it soon leads to shocking revelations that suggest it is somehow linked to the Charlie Courage affair. The grim discoveries of the unfolding investigation lead Banks in a direction he does not wish to go: the past and private world of his most powerful enemy, Chief Constable Riddle.

line: The year is 1943 and life is good for Jewel Hilburn, her husband, Leston, and their five children. Although there's a war on, the Mississippi economy is booming, providing plenty of business for the hardworking family. And even the news that eldest son James has enlisted is mitigated by the fact that Jewel, now pushing 40, is pregnant with one last child. Her joy is slightly clouded, however, when her childhood friend Cathedral arrives at the door with a troubling prophecy: "I say unto you that the baby you be carrying be yo' hardship, be yo' test in this world. This be my prophesying unto you, Miss Jewel." When the child is finally born, it seems that Cathedral's prediction was empty: the baby appears normal in every way. As the months go by, however, Jewel becomes increasingly afraid that something is wrong with little Brenda Kay—she doesn't cry, she doesn't roll over, she's hardly ever awake. Eventually husband and wife take the baby to the doctor and are informed that she is a "Mongolian Idiot," not expected to live past the age of 2. Jewel angrily rebuffs the doctor's suggestion that they institutionalize Brenda Kay. Instead the Hilburns shoulder the burdens—and discover the unexpected joys—of living with a Down syndrome child.

line: Without disclosing too much personal info, I’m in my mid twenties and I work with people with disabilities for a living. Not many with autism, but a few. I watch a lot of YouTube and read lots of articles and blogs on disabilities and disorders to try and keep myself well informed so I can help disabled/disordered people and their support teams to the best of my ability. I recently started researching autism because I felt I needed to know more than what I learned in college and wow...I am 65-70% certain I might be autistic. I feel relief and terror at the same time? What’s really freaking me out is if I am autistic I want to know for sure, however I don’t want to force it if I’m not. I had always accredited my quirks and social struggles to my alternative/religious upbringing, but all I’ve learned so far resonates so much with me. I don’t know why I’m posting this or what my question is, but I would sincerely appreciate any commentary you all may have if you read this far.

The two leads, Anna and Claire, argue over Claire's new found "Love" while Anna's Scottish maid, Catherine, is brought to tears by her employer's harsh verbal rebukes. Things get tense as Anna, a mistress to a wealthy gentleman, tries to talk Claire out of her profession of love for another: a young woman. Claire, on the other hand, has already made plans with her young love to meet at Anna's house in the hopes that she will be able to persuade her new love to engage in a "vile assignation." Things go awry, however, when the girl arrives and recognizes that an emerald necklace that Anna is wearing belongs to her mother. The plot line focuses on whether Anna and Claire will be able to find a way to hold on to both the girl and her wealthy but unfaithful father. The play is delivered through quick, witty Victorian-era dialogue, mixed with double entendres and vernacular expressions, to explore the relationship between the two women and their maid. Through humor and nuance, the play explores the negotiation, conflict, compromise and reconciliation that arise in their relationship.

next_line: Mr Mandelson, a former Labour communications director, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "I understand why the Tories will be gunning for Alastair Campbell because they fear his campaigning skills. "What I understand less is why the BBC should be joining with the Tories in driving that agenda. "In my experience of these things, parties which shout about dirty tricks and the like tend to do so because they fear a direct hit in some vulnerable part of their political anatomy. "I suggest the BBC concentrates on the issues and helps the public to understand the policies and the choices that are at stake in the election rather than engages in the process politics, the trivialisation of the campaign. "I think the BBC would be much better advised to leave all this stuff well alone, concentrate on the issues as I say, not resume their demonisation of Alastair Campbell - we all know where that led before."

line: The Nokia-sponsored research showed that mobiles and fixed phones were used for different purposes. Home phones were used for longer calls but conversations on mobiles tended to be shorter, between mobiles and to friends. In the UK 69% of those questioned said they turned to their fixed phone because it was still cheaper to use than a mobile. However, when pressed few could say with accuracy how tariffs on fixed and mobile phones compared. In the US and Germany many of those interviewed said they used the fixed phone because it was more reliable than a mobile handset and let them get access to the net at relatively high speeds. In all the countries where interviews were carried out, older people were more likely to use a fixed line phone more than a mobile. Women aged 50 or above almost never use a mobile phone, the research found.
previous_line: Research by handset maker Nokia shows that more and more people are using their mobile phone for every call they make or take. According to the study, more than 45 million people in the UK, Germany, US and South Korea now only use a mobile. It showed that people keep their fixed line phone because call charges are lower, but most of those questioned said the future was definitely mobile.
next_line: The move to mobile was most pronounced in South Korea where 65% of those questioned said they already make most of their calls from a mobile. 18% said they would not get a landline if they moved house.

line: Agriculture Minister Adamu Bello said the scheme aimed to boost production from an expected 180,000 tonnes this year to 600,000 tonnes by 2008. The government will pump 154m naira ($1.1m; £591,000) into subsidies for farming chemicals and seedlings. Nigeria is currently the world's fourth-largest cocoa producer.
previous_line: The government of Nigeria is hoping to triple cocoa production over the next three years with the launch of an ambitious development programme.
next_line: Cocoa was the main export product in Nigeria during the 1960s. But with the coming of oil, the government began to pay less attention to the cocoa sector and production began to fall from a peak of about 400,000 tonnes a year in 1970. At the launch of the programme in the south-western city of Ibadan, Mr Bello explained that an additional aim of the project is to encourage the processing of cocoa in the country and lift local consumption. He also announced that 91m naira of the funding available had been earmarked for establishing cocoa plant nurseries. The country could be looking to emulate rival Ghana, which produced a bumper crop last year. However, some farmers are sceptical about the proposals. "People who are not farming will hijack the subsidy," said Joshua Osagie, a cocoa farmer from Edo state told Reuters. "The farmers in the village never see any assistance," he added.

line: Holmes hit the front just before the bell in front of a sell-out crowd in Glasgow and cruised to victory in a time of four minutes 14.74 seconds. "It was nice to get that out of the way. I was nervous about whether I would actually be able to get round. "I felt good. I just had to relax and use my racing knowledge," said Holmes. "It was all about winning in front of my home crowd. The time is irrelevant. "I got round in one piece and didn't disgrace myself. Now it's about going forward. "The reception I've had since the Olympics has been amazing and that's why I wanted to keep running this year, because I get a buzz from the crowd." Holmes ran a tactically perfect race to finish clear of France's Hind Dehiba and Russia's Svetlana Cherkasova. The Olympic 800m and 1500m champion's time was inside the qualifying mark for the European Indoor Championships in Madrid in March. But the 34-year-old would not reveal whether she intended to run or not, having previously indicated she would leave a decision until after the Birmingham Grand Prix on 18 February.
previous_line: Britain's Kelly Holmes marked her first appearance on home soil since winning double Olympic gold with 1500m victory at the Norwich Union International.
